text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mostly firmer in quiet trade. Front month August added $2.20 to close at $315.00 per tonne, while October lost $0.20 to close at $304.60 per tonne. Volume was thin and trading extremely quiet. France and the United Kingdom had rains over the weekend which have brought some relief although more rains are needed for a satisfactory emergence of the crop.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed higher across the board as prices retraced some of the losses made during the previous session. Today's action focused on rolling of May positions. May added 9 points to close at 11.55 cents/lb, while July closed 7 points higher at 11.14 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 9 and 11 points.

PERU - Sugar production in Peru in 1998 is forecast to reach 680,000 tonne, tel quel, up from 641,500 tonnes expected for 1997 and 607,800 tonnes produced in 1996. Sugar consumption in 1998 is forecast to reach 775,000 tonnes, up from 760,000 tonnes in 1997 and 745,000 tonnes in 1996. Molasses production in 1998 is put at 279,000 tonnes, up from 263,015 tonnes in 1997 and 243,120 tonnes in 1996.

BRAZIL - Sugar production in March 1997 amounted to 223,100 tonnes, raw value, up from 199,800 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative production in the first eleven months of 1996/97 (May/March) up to 14.659 mn tonnes against 13.651 mn tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total production in 1995/96 reached 13.661 mn tonnes against 12.598 mn tonnes in 1994/95.

Total output in the Center South in May/March 1996/97 amounted to 11.325 mn tonnes, while the balance was produced in the North/Northeast. Total alcohol output in May/March 1996/97 hit 14.310 bn litres of which 12.112 bn in the Center South and 2.198 bn litres in the North/Northeast. Total hydrous alcohol production in May/March 1996/97 reached 9.742 bn litres while anhydrous alcohol output amounted to 4.568 bn litres.

MALAYSIA - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 88,597 tonnes, raw value, down from 92,450 tonnes imported in December 1995. This brought total imports in calendar year 1996 up to 1.093 mn tonnes against 1.033 mn tonnes in 1995 and 959,518 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in calendar year 1996 were Australia with 579,997 tonnes raws against 628,445 tonnes, Thailand with 371,600 tonnes, up from 274,205 tonnes and Fiji with 75,983 tonnes against 104,450 tonnes.

Sugar exports in December 1996 reached 7,411 tonnes, down from 12,723 tonnes in December 1995. This brought total exports in calendar year 1996 up to 105,937 tonnes against 123,561 tonnes in 1995 and 159,525 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of destination in January/December 1996 were Singapore with 62,263 tonnes whites and Indonesia with 25,398 tonnes.

DENMARK - Sugar exports in January 1997 amounted to 10,394 tonnes, raw value, hardly changed from last year's 11,941 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in October/January 1996/97 up to 60,143 tonnes compared to 54,587 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 173,004 tonnes against 199,559 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in October/January 1996/97 were Norway with 31,669 tonnes whites against 39,802 tonnes, Libya with 15,400 tonnes against nil and Iceland with 3,597 tonnes against 2,899 tonnes. Sugar imports in October/January 1996/97 reached 17,569 tonnes, up from 3,287 tonnes in 1995/96. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Germany with 8,872 tonnes whites against 2,669 tonnes and Sweden with 6,814 tonnes against 18 tonnes.

UNITED STATES - Sugar imports under the 1996/97 (October/September) tariff rate quota up to April 6, 1997 amounted to 825,681 tonnes, raw value. This is equivalent to 43.46 per cent of the total quota of 1.90 million tonnes.
